reason: No cited evidence is provided for any of the key premises. The claims about deformation behavior, annealing response, microstructural evolution, and property trade-offs in this specific alloy are unsupported by prior data.
premises: Heavy cold rolling induces high dislocation density and grain refinement, increasing strength but reducing ductility in NbZrTiHfMo.
Post-deformation annealing at ~700 °C for 20 min causes partial recovery and limited necklace recrystallization.
Partial recovery/recrystallization relieves localized stresses and improves plasticity without eliminating solid-solution strengthening and residual dislocation structures.
The annealed condition retains compressive yield strength close to the as-cast 1719 MPa while increasing compressive plasticity over the cold-rolled state.
The effect is specific to the 700 °C/20 min window; lower temperatures give insufficient recovery, higher temperatures cause full recrystallization and strength loss.
